Covert
KUV-ert
noun
From the Old French covert, the past participle of covrir, to cover — Latin cooperire. A covert is a covered place: a thicket, a shelter, a hiding place. The modern sense of secret is a later development from the same root.

Biblical Definition

A covert is a covered place, and Scripture uses it for every kind of shelter from the mildest to the most exalted. It is a feature of the landscape: Abigail came down “by the covert of the hill” (1Sa 25:20), riding to meet David with her loaves and her wisdom just where the ground hid her approach. It is a piece of temple architecture — “the covert for the sabbath that they had built in the house” (2Ki 16:18), which Ahaz stripped away for the king of Assyria, a small sentence recording a large apostasy. It is a duty owed to refugees: “Let mine outcasts dwell with thee, Moab; be thou a covert to them from the face of the spoiler” (Isa 16:4). And it rises to its great uses in the mouth of faith. The psalmist says, “I will trust in the covert of thy wings” (Psa 61:4), taking shelter not under a hill but under God Himself. Isaiah promises a tabernacle “for a covert from storm and from rain” (Isa 4:6), and then makes the covert a man: “a man shall be as an hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the tempest” (Isa 32:2). That is the word’s destination. The shelter Israel needed was finally not a thicket, a roof, or a wing, but a Person — and He stands in the open weather Himself to be one.

Webster 1828 Definition

A covered or sheltering place: a thicket, a shelter from storm, a hiding place. Used of landscape, of architecture, of the wings of God, and at last of a man.

expand to see more

COVERT, n. A covering, shelter, or defense; a place of protection.

A thicket; a shady place; a hiding place for game.

From the Old French covert, past participle of covrir, to cover; Latin cooperire.

COVERT, adj. Covered; hid; secret; disguised — a later sense of the same word.

In Scripture, a shelter from storm, tempest, or the face of the spoiler (Isa 4:6; Isa 16:4).

Key Scripture

1Sa 25:20 — "And it was so, as she rode on the ass, that she came down by the covert of the hill, and, behold, David and his men came down against her; and she met them."

Psa 61:4 — "I will abide in thy tabernacle for ever: I will trust in the covert of thy wings. Selah."

Isa 4:6 — "And there shall be a tabernacle for a shadow in the daytime from the heat, and for a place of refuge, and for a covert from storm and from rain."

Isa 32:2 — "And a man shall be as an hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the tempest; as rivers of water in a dry place, as the shadow of a great rock in a weary land."

Modern Corruption

Isa 32:2 is regularly softened into a promise that Christ shelters us from difficulty, when the verse describes a man who becomes a covert by standing in the weather himself.

expand to see more

The corruption is the sheltered-life reading. Isa 32:2 is a favourite verse for consolation, and it is commonly preached as though it promised that the Christian, being in Christ, will be kept out of the wind and the tempest altogether. The grammar will not bear it. The verse says a man shall be as an hiding place from the wind — the shelter is a person, and a person who shelters others is by definition standing in what they are sheltered from. The wind does not stop; it is intercepted. Read the chapter and this becomes plain: the promise is given to a people who will still know storm, and the mercy offered is not the abolition of weather but a covert in the middle of it.

Recover the plain sense: Christ is the man of Isa 32:2, and the cross is what it costs to be a hiding place. He was not spared the wind; He met it, and the darkness at noon was the tempest breaking on Him rather than on His people. That truth also converts the verse into a pattern for His servants. A pastor, a father, a friend who intends to be a covert to anyone must expect to stand where the weather is, and the measure of the shelter he gives will be the measure of what strikes him instead. Set beside it Psa 61:4 and Isa 16:4, and the duty is complete — hide yourself under the wings of God, and be a covert to the outcast at your own door.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old French covert, covered — a sheltering place; from thicket and wing to the Man who is a covert from the tempest.

expand to see more

Covert — Old French covert, past participle of covrir, to cover.

Latin cooperire, to cover over; the adjectival sense secret is later.

Of landscape: the covert of the hill (1Sa 25:20).

Of God: the covert of thy wings (Psa 61:4).

Of a man: a covert from the tempest (Isa 32:2) — shelter by interception.

Usage

"Isa 32:2 makes the shelter a Person standing in the weather, not a removal from it."

"Isa 16:4 makes providing covert to the outcast a duty laid even upon Moab."

"2Ki 16:18: Ahaz removed the sabbath covert for the king of Assyria — apostasy in a detail."
